A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LAMER study, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Sokoban, MineSweeper, Webshop and ALFWorld, including performance comparisons, generalization tests, ablations and additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including Tables 1–5, the behavioral analyses and the trajectory example in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same cross-episode training objective, discounted credit assignment and in-context adaptation through self-reflection. No algorithmic component, input, output or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four environments, harder Sokoban and MineSweeper scenarios, and ALFWorld in-distribution and held-out task categories. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Zero-shot, ReAct, Reflexion, PPO, RLOO, GRPO and GiGPO. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the ALFWorld comparison and Appendix D, including GiGPO with and without inter-episode memory.

E3.justification: The pass@1–3 evaluation, model configurations, task splits and training settings are identical. Both versions retain three episodes with group size eight for Meta-RL versus group size 24 for standard RL.

E4.justification: The trajectory-diversity analysis, harder-task and distribution-shift tests, discount-factor sweep, memory ablations and training-cost analysis are unchanged. Appendix D.2's memory-enabled baseline analysis and Appendix E's case study are also retained.

E5.justification: No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-reporting information is added or revised. The trajectory-diversity boxplots and other statistical reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported results in Tables 1–5 and the empirical figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains LAMER pass@3 scores of 55.9%, 74.4% and 89.1% on Sokoban, MineSweeper and Webshop, respectively.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, assumptions, return definitions and Equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. The isolated endpoint-label edits in Figure 2 do not revise a stated mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about inducing exploration through Meta-RL, improving test-time adaptation and scaling, and generalizing to harder or unseen tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration, discount factors and reflection-only memory are identical. Both versions retain the sequential-rollout training-cost limitation and the same discussion of generalization boundaries and future work.

D1.justification: The implementation information in Section 5.1 and Appendices A–C is unchanged, including prompts, optimizer settings, learning rate, batch sizes, epochs, temperatures and token limits. The code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning in Section 2 are unchanged. The added conference-publication header does not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The body prose, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives small spacing and alignment adjustments; its final-episode endpoint labels change from s_{T-1}^{(N-1)} to s_T^{(N-1)} in both rows. Publication-header text is added, while the other figures, tables and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific text, experimental evidence, analyses and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The publication header and localized Figure 2 edits do not produce a meaningful net change in clarity, scientific support or overall paper quality.
